purpose: Refresh the public repeated-inference frontier for raw/token divergence that could propagate into deterministic evaluation scores or paired signs.

sources.observation: A live vLLM serving engine with one LoRA adapter under greedy decoding produced 2-4 distinct byte outputs across 16 byte-identical requests in many fast execution arms. A specific fp32-eager-cuBLAS interior produced 64+/64+ byte-identical serving calls and repeated 40-request sweeps. The issue reports same-server run-to-run output flips but does not publish the per-call raw outputs; probe logs are described as available on request.
sources.scope: Strong evidence that full serving context can introduce run-to-run output divergence even when isolated kernel/offline probes are clean. It does not yet quantify token divergence to deterministic score or paired-sign divergence because the raw output set is not published in the issue body.

sources.observation: Under temperature=0 and batch-invariant mode, EAGLE speculative decoding and non-EAGLE execution produced token sequences that diverged from the first token; the issue publishes both token sequences.
sources.scope: This proves token-level propagation across two engine configurations, not run-to-run divergence under one frozen fingerprint, so it is not a same-fingerprint mismatch-rate sample.

sources.observation: Five repeats of a byte-identical concurrent workload under one unchanged server process showed non-identical logprobs at high co-residency while generated token IDs remained identical in the reported reproducer.
sources.scope: Demonstrates that response/logprob mismatch can fail to propagate to token mismatch; full-output mismatch must not be used as a proxy for score/sign mismatch.

measurement_rule_update: Track response/logprob, token/text, deterministic score bit, paired score pair, and oriented sign Z as separate layers.
Do not count cross-configuration token divergence as a same-fingerprint stochastic-repeat trial.
Do not infer score/sign divergence from byte-output divergence when the actual outputs or scorer results are unavailable.
A public same-fingerprint trace with raw divergent outputs plus a deterministic task scorer remains the preferred missing artifact.
frontier: Find or generate a public same-fingerprint repeated-inference trace that exposes the divergent raw/token outputs and a deterministic scorer contract, then measure raw->token->score->paired-sign propagation without pseudoreplication.
